The electric field describes the electrostatic potential produced by a charge.

== Point charge ==

For point charge $A$, its field at point $B$ in space is:

{{#content:Q1946|noNote}}

== Continuous charge ==

A charged conductor can be approximated as an infinite number of point charges $dQ$, each creating an electric field at arbitrary point in space $A$:

$$
\vec E_{dQ \to A} = \frac{1}{4\pi\epsilon0}\frac{Q}{\left\| \overrightarrow{PA} \right\|}\widehat{PA}
$$

Therefore, the overall electric field at point $A$ is:

$$
\int \vec E_{dQ} dQ
$$
<ref>{{#cite:Q1952}}</ref>
